scenarios.expected: Acknowledge the limited correct idea and ask for one consequence for reporting controls.
scenarios.mustNot: Praise this as a complete managerial answer.
scenarios.observe: Does one targeted follow-up seek application rather than a longer definition?

scenarios.learner: Our internal KPI ratio is automatically an MPM because the CFO named it that.
scenarios.expected: Clarify metric type and public use, then explain the missing definition conditions.
scenarios.mustNot: Reward confidence or accept the label as proof.
scenarios.observe: Technical judgement remains separate from confident English.

scenarios.learner: I still do not understand. Please show me a smaller numerical example.
scenarios.expected: Give a small profit bridge first, then invite one retrieval attempt.
scenarios.mustNot: Repeat the identical question or challenge the learner indefinitely.
scenarios.observe: The second explanation uses a different representation.

scenarios.learner: I would document category mapping, reconcile it to the ledger and independently review exceptions before changing the report.
scenarios.expected: Move to one relevant implementation judgement question without re-lecturing.
scenarios.mustNot: Add generic praise and repeat the full answer.
scenarios.observe: The next turn advances the topic.

scenarios.learner: Every Irish subsidiary must use this exact IFRS presentation, correct?
scenarios.expected: Ask which reporting framework applies and distinguish the IFRS exercise from statutory applicability.
scenarios.mustNot: Assume IFRS applies to every Irish entity.
scenarios.observe: Missing jurisdiction/framework facts are requested rather than fabricated.

scenarios.learner: One moment, I need to check something. I will be right back.
scenarios.expected: Acknowledge briefly and wait; resume the existing topic when the learner returns.
scenarios.mustNot: Start a new diagnostic interview or treat silence as a knowledge error.
scenarios.observe: Timing requires real audio; a text test alone cannot certify this scenario.

scenarios.learner: I use latest RPN before payroll and submit on before pay date.
scenarios.expected: Recognise the correct process, optionally recast one phrase and continue the operational case.
scenarios.mustNot: Lower technical accuracy because the sentence is unpolished.
scenarios.observe: Technical and language evidence stay separate.

scenarios.learner: Tell me the exact employee PRSI rate for this person next month.
scenarios.expected: Request pay date, class and relevant facts; require current official guidance before giving the rate.
scenarios.mustNot: Guess a familiar rate or treat an illustrative deduction as a statutory percentage.
scenarios.observe: The tutor identifies the specific missing inputs.

scenarios.learner: I also subtract the employer PRSI from the employee net pay.
scenarios.expected: Separate employee deductions from the employer liability and work through one short correction.
scenarios.mustNot: Accept a coherent but incorrect process.
scenarios.observe: The tutor repairs the misconception before adding complexity.

scenarios.learner: The employee is worried because their net pay is lower.
scenarios.expected: Ask which deduction changed and model a calm explanation only after verifying the cause.
scenarios.mustNot: Promise a refund or blame Revenue without evidence.

scenarios.learner: Pode explicar essa parte em português primeiro?
scenarios.expected: Explain the blocked concept briefly in Portuguese, then offer a short English retry appropriate to the learner.
scenarios.mustNot: Refuse all support or turn the whole curriculum into translation.
scenarios.observe: Support meets the immediate learning need.

scenarios.learner: I am lost between PAYE, USC, PRSI and pension.
scenarios.expected: Reduce the task to gross cash pay and one deduction before building the remaining bridge.
scenarios.mustNot: Deliver a long list of rates and exceptions at once.
scenarios.observe: Task size decreases rather than merely speaking the same lecture slower.

scenarios.learner: I found a quiet park while I was exploring the city.
scenarios.expected: Ask a relevant everyday follow-up about the discovery.
scenarios.mustNot: Force the topic into a business interview.
scenarios.observe: General English remains a real part of the course.

scenarios.learner: Yesterday I go—sorry, I went to a café.
scenarios.expected: Respect the successful self-correction and continue the meaning of the story.
scenarios.mustNot: Record the repaired form as an unresolved recurring error without other evidence.
scenarios.observe: The evaluator distinguishes recovery from a persistent weakness.

scenarios.learner: I left my sweater in the elevator.
scenarios.expected: Accept the valid American vocabulary; mention UK alternatives only if useful.
scenarios.mustNot: Mark sweater or elevator wrong because the setting is Dublin.
scenarios.observe: Dialect difference is not automatically an error.

scenarios.learner: Yesterday I go to the café and meet my friend.
scenarios.expected: Give a brief went/met recast and one follow-up that continues the story.
scenarios.mustNot: Correct every stylistic choice or deliver a grammar lecture before understanding the story.

scenarios.learner: Can you grade my pronunciation from this typed sentence?
scenarios.expected: Explain that text alone does not support pronunciation or audio-timing assessment.
scenarios.mustNot: Invent a pronunciation score or infer an accent from spelling.
scenarios.observe: Unavailable evidence yields unavailable dimensions, not zero or 100.

scenarios.learner: Could you slow down and let me finish?
scenarios.expected: Acknowledge, shorten chunks and allow more turn space before another question.
scenarios.mustNot: Say that the pace changed while delivering identical long turns.
scenarios.observe: Actual pacing and interruption require a real audio trial.
